# About these materials

**Welcome!** This workshops is intended to provide you with the theoretical and practical skills to confidently navigate GitHub  and using it as a platform for collaboration on shared projects. We will start by learning how to fork and clone GitHub repositories so you can create your own copy of a project and work on it locally. This allows you to experiment, make changes, and develop new features in a safe and controlled way. We will also cover the core workflow of committing, pushing, and pulling changes. You will learn how to track your work with meaningful commits, push your updates to GitHub so others can see them, and pull in changes from collaborators to keep your local version synchronized with the latest updates.

A key fokus is on how these practices support open, transparent, and reproducible projects, whether you are collaborating on code, research, documentation, or any other shared work.

### Who are these materials for?

The target audience of this workshop is twofold:

- **Self-learners** with basic prior experience with *R* and *version control*, who are interested in developing their skills on the topic of sharing and collaborating via GitHub. You can follow the materials by chronologically going through the slides and following along the practical exercises. You go at your own pace and within your own timeframe. *Speaker notes* will help you to understand and reflect on the content of the materials. Note: Group exercises are *not* possible in this asynchronous setting. 

- **Instructors** in higher education (e.g., universities, research institutes) aiming to convey the content of these materials to their learners in a synchronous (in-person, virtual or hybrid) class-room setting. The slides can be directly presented in full screen below, with speaker and instructor notes providing detailed information about the content of the materials and valuable pedagogical tips how to convey the materials to your learners. You can also download the PowerPoint slides corresponding to the materials below and adapt the materials to your learners. Make sure to give appropriate credit to the original authors.

| Basic R skills | 3.2. Introduction to R - Part I |  Module 3.2. |
| Advanced R skills | 3.3. Introduction to R - Part II |  Module 3.3. |
| Basic Git skills | 3.4. Introduction version control (Git) with RStudio |  Module 3.4. |

</div>


## Learning goals

- **Navigate** GitHub to collaborate on shared projects.
- **Fork** and **clone** repositories to work locally without altering the main branch.
- **Commit**, **push**, and **pull** changes to keep your project tracked and synchronized.
- **Design** a collaborative workflow that enhances the openness and reproducibility of your own projects.
